items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Reading Books” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Reading Books

Books open doors to knowledge, imagination and understanding. A reader can learn about distant places, meet characters from different backgrounds and explore ideas that may not appear in a classroom lesson. Reading is therefore both useful and enjoyable.

Different books serve different purposes. Textbooks explain school subjects, while stories help us imagine how other people feel. Biographies introduce the lives and efforts of individuals, and science books encourage us to ask questions about the world. A newspaper or a reference book can also help us find information, although we should check important claims against reliable sources.

Regular reading develops vocabulary and improves writing. It teaches us to concentrate and gives us time away from the constant noise of screens. A library makes this habit affordable because many readers can share the same books. Students should choose age-appropriate books, look after them and return borrowed copies on time.

I try to read for a short period each day. When a word is unfamiliar, I note it down and look up its meaning. Later I discuss an interesting passage with a friend. Reading does not mean accepting every idea without thought; it means considering ideas carefully and asking questions. In this way books become companions as well as teachers. A steady reading habit can enrich our lives for many years.

items.text: Write a short composition on “Tree Plantation” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
Tree Plantation

Trees are essential to a healthy environment. They provide shade, shelter for wildlife and useful products such as fruit and timber. Their roots help hold soil in place, while their leaves contribute to the natural processes that support life. Planting and protecting trees is therefore an important responsibility.

In many places trees are cut down to make room for roads, buildings or farms. Some development is necessary, but careless removal can leave land exposed to erosion and reduce habitats for birds and other animals. In hot weather, a tree-lined playground or street can also offer welcome shade. Planting suitable trees can help restore some of these benefits.

A successful plantation requires more than putting a sapling in the ground. We should choose species suited to the local environment and plant them in places where their roots and branches have enough space. A teacher, gardener or local expert can help select an appropriate site. Young trees need water, protection and regular attention, especially during dry weather.

Schools can organise supervised planting days and prepare a watering schedule. Communities can also protect existing trees and replace those lost to storms or disease. Everyone can take part by caring for a plant or learning why local species matter. If we combine careful planting with long-term care, the trees we nurture today can benefit future generations.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Journey by Train” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Journey by Train

A journey by train can be both comfortable and memorable. Last winter I travelled with my family to visit relatives in another town. It was my first long train journey, and I was excited from the moment we reached the station.

The platform was busy with passengers carrying bags and looking for their coaches. We checked our tickets and waited safely behind the platform edge. When the train arrived, we found our seats and placed our luggage where it would not block the aisle. Soon the train began to move, and the station slowly disappeared from view.

Through the window I saw fields, ponds and small houses. At some stations people got on while others waved goodbye to their families. My mother shared snacks, and my father pointed out a river as we crossed a bridge. I enjoyed watching the changing landscape and talking with my younger brother. We also made sure not to throw any waste out of the window.

The journey took several hours, but I did not feel bored. When we reached our destination, our relatives were waiting to welcome us. The trip taught me that a journey is not merely a way to reach a place; it can also be a chance to observe people, enjoy nature and spend time with family.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Duties of a Student” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Duties of a Student

Student life is a time for learning, building good habits and discovering interests. A student's main duty is to study sincerely, but education includes much more than memorising lessons for examinations. It also involves responsibility towards family, school and the wider community.

A responsible student attends classes regularly, listens carefully and asks questions when a lesson is unclear. Preparing a realistic timetable helps balance schoolwork, rest and recreation. Students should complete their own work honestly instead of using unfair means. A mistake is an opportunity to learn, and teachers can help when a topic is difficult.

Good behaviour matters as well. We should respect teachers, parents and classmates, and we should never make fun of someone who learns differently. Keeping the classroom clean and taking care of shared books show respect for school property. During group work, students can listen to different opinions and share tasks fairly.

Students also need exercise, adequate sleep and time for creative activities. Joining a club or taking part in a supervised community project can develop cooperation and confidence. Above all, learning should help us become thoughtful and kind citizens. By doing our duties regularly, we prepare ourselves not only for examinations but also for the responsibilities of adult life.

items.text: Write a short composition on “Physical Exercise” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
Physical Exercise

Physical exercise is an important part of a healthy life. It keeps the body active and can help us feel refreshed. Walking, cycling, swimming and playing games are examples of exercise, and different people may enjoy different activities.

Regular movement helps develop strength and fitness. Team games can also teach cooperation, patience and respect for rules. Exercise gives students a break from long hours of sitting and studying. It can be more enjoyable when friends or family members participate together. However, exercise alone is not enough: healthy food, safe drinking water and sufficient sleep are important too.

We should choose activities that suit our age and health. Beginners can start gently and gradually increase their activity. It is wise to warm up, use appropriate equipment and drink water when needed. Playing in a safe place and following a coach's instructions can reduce the risk of injury. Anyone with an illness or medical concern should ask a qualified health professional for advice.

I enjoy walking and playing badminton with my friends. These activities make me feel energetic and help me return to my studies with a clear mind. The best routine is one that is safe and enjoyable enough to follow regularly. By making room for movement in our daily lives, we can support our physical and mental well-being.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Book Fair” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Book Fair

A book fair brings readers, writers and publishers together. It offers a pleasant opportunity to discover books, share ideas and celebrate the habit of reading. I visited a book fair with my classmates and a teacher last year, and the experience remains fresh in my mind.

The fair was held in a large open area with rows of colourful stalls. Publishers displayed storybooks, poems, children's magazines and books on science and history. Visitors moved from stall to stall, examining covers and discussing their favourite authors. Some stalls had small spaces where writers spoke to readers about their work.

I was especially interested in a collection of short stories. Before buying it, I read the description and compared its price with another edition. My friend chose a book about birds, while our teacher recommended a biography for the school library. We also attended a reading session where a writer answered questions from children.

A book fair is more than a place to buy things. It encourages people to explore new ideas and helps young readers develop curiosity. Those who cannot buy many books can still discover titles to look for in a library. We returned home tired but happy, carrying books and many ideas to discuss. I hope to visit another fair soon.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Clean Water” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Clean Water

Clean water is essential for life. People need safe water for drinking, cooking and personal hygiene, and farmers need it to grow crops. Animals and plants also depend on water, so protecting water sources benefits the whole environment.

Water can become polluted when rubbish, sewage or harmful chemicals enter rivers, ponds and other sources. Drinking contaminated water can cause illness. For this reason families should use a safe supply and follow local health guidance on treating water when necessary. Storing drinking water in clean, covered containers also helps protect it from contamination.

Everyone can help reduce waste and pollution. We can turn off taps after use, report leaking pipes and avoid throwing plastic or other rubbish into water. Communities and local authorities have important roles in managing waste, protecting sources and maintaining safe water systems. Schools can teach students how water reaches their homes and why cleanliness matters.

During a flood or other emergency, a normally safe source may become contaminated. In such circumstances we should listen to reliable local advice rather than assume the water is safe. Clean water should be available to everyone, not treated as a luxury. By using it carefully and working together to protect it, we support health, farming and the natural world.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A School Garden” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A School Garden

A school garden is a place where students can learn about plants while making their surroundings attractive. Our school has a small garden beside the playground. Teachers and students work together to care for it, and it has become one of my favourite places.

At the beginning of the term we prepared the soil with the help of a gardener. We planted flower seeds and a few vegetables in separate beds. Each group received a simple task, such as watering, removing weeds or keeping a record of growth. Our science teacher explained why plants need suitable light, water and soil.

The garden is useful in several ways. Students can observe leaves, flowers and insects rather than learning about them only from pictures. Working in a group teaches us patience and cooperation. The flowers make the school cheerful, while the vegetables show how food can be grown. We avoid damaging nests or insects and ask an adult before using any gardening tools.

A garden needs regular care, including during holidays. For this reason we make a schedule and ask school staff to supervise the work. I enjoy watching a seedling grow over several weeks. Our garden reminds us that a small effort, repeated patiently, can create something beautiful and useful.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Value of Time” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Value of Time

Time is one of the most valuable resources in life. Once a moment has passed, we cannot bring it back. Learning to use time wisely helps students complete their duties while still leaving room for rest, friendship and enjoyment.

A timetable is a useful guide, but it should be realistic. We can set aside time for school lessons, homework, exercise and sleep. Difficult tasks may be divided into smaller steps so that they do not feel overwhelming. Starting revision early can reduce pressure before an examination. When plans change, we can adjust them instead of giving up altogether.

Using time well does not mean working without a break. Rest and recreation are necessary for health and concentration. The problem arises when an activity continues so long that important duties are repeatedly neglected. For example, setting a reasonable limit on screen use can leave more time for reading or playing outdoors.

Punctuality also shows respect for other people's time. Arriving on time for school and keeping promises help build trust. At the same time, we should be understanding when someone faces circumstances beyond their control. By planning carefully and choosing our priorities, we can make each day more balanced and meaningful.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Rainy Day” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Rainy Day

A rainy day brings a special change to the familiar landscape. Dark clouds gather, the air becomes cooler and the sound of falling rain fills the surroundings. Some people enjoy the change, while others face difficulties travelling or working outdoors.

One morning last monsoon, rain began just as I was preparing for school. I carried an umbrella and walked carefully along the wet road with my neighbour. Trees looked freshly washed, and small drops hung from their leaves. At school many students arrived with wet shoes, but our teachers made sure we entered the classrooms safely.

Rain is valuable for farming and for replenishing water in ponds and rivers. Yet heavy rainfall can also cause waterlogging and make roads slippery. People who work outside may lose income when they cannot work. We should therefore appreciate the rain while remembering those who need help during difficult weather.

After school I stayed indoors, read a story and listened to the rain on the roof. In the evening the clouds cleared and the garden looked bright again. That day reminded me of both the beauty and the responsibilities that come with the rainy season. Keeping drains clear and following local safety advice can help our communities cope better when rain is heavy.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Village Market” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Village Market

A village market is an important meeting place for people in the countryside. It is usually held once or twice a week in an open space. Farmers, shopkeepers and customers come from neighbouring villages.

At the market, vegetables, fish, fruit and household goods are arranged in separate areas. Some sellers sit under temporary roofs, while others spread their goods on mats. Buyers compare prices and choose what they need. The calls of vendors and the conversations of customers make the place lively.

The market also gives neighbours a chance to exchange news and meet people they do not see every day. Prices may change with the season, so families must plan their spending. Treating sellers and buyers fairly makes this busy gathering more useful to everyone.

The market helps farmers sell their produce without travelling to a distant town. It also gives small traders an opportunity to earn a living. However, waste and muddy paths can cause inconvenience. Proper bins, clean water and regular cleaning would make the market safer and more pleasant. A well-managed village market serves both the local economy and the community.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A School Library” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A School Library

A school library is a quiet place where students can read and borrow books. It is an important part of a school because learning should not be limited to textbooks. A good library encourages curiosity and independent study.

Our library has shelves of stories, biographies, dictionaries and books on science and history. Students can consult reference books when preparing a project. The librarian helps us find suitable books and keeps a record of those we borrow. There are tables where we can sit and read during free periods.

A library can also include books for different reading levels and interests. Students who find reading difficult may benefit from guidance and time to choose a suitable book. A welcoming collection allows more children to discover that reading can be a pleasure, not just a school task.

We must follow some simple rules. We should speak softly, handle books carefully and return them on time. Writing on pages or tearing them prevents others from enjoying the same books. A reading club can make the library even more welcoming by allowing students to share their favourite stories. A useful library helps build thoughtful readers and makes school life richer.

items.text: Write a short composition on “My Favourite Hobby” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
My Favourite Hobby

My favourite hobby is gardening. It gives me pleasure and teaches me to be patient. I do not need a large field; a few pots on a balcony or a small patch of soil can be enough to begin.

I grow flowers and some vegetables with help from my family. First, I loosen the soil and choose healthy seeds or seedlings. I water the plants when they need it and remove weeds carefully. Sometimes insects damage the leaves, so I ask an experienced gardener for safe advice rather than using chemicals carelessly.

I keep a small notebook to record what I plant and how it grows. This helps me remember which pots receive enough sunlight. When I share extra seedlings with a neighbour, my hobby becomes a way to build friendship as well as care for nature.

The most exciting moment comes when a seedling produces its first flower or fruit. Not every plant survives, but a failure helps me learn about sunlight, water and soil. Gardening also makes our surroundings greener. It gives me a useful break from study and reminds me that living things need steady care. I hope to continue this hobby as I grow older.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Journey by Boat” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Journey by Boat

Last autumn I went on a boat journey with my family. We visited relatives who live across a river. The sky was clear, and the water shone in the morning sunlight.

Before boarding, we checked that the boat was not overcrowded and followed the boatman's instructions. I sat beside my mother and watched the banks move slowly past us. Fishermen were working in small boats, and children waved from near their homes. Green fields and patches of trees stretched beyond the water.

At one point a larger vessel passed at a distance, and our boat rocked gently in its wake. I held the side of my seat and listened to the boatman. He knew the route well, and his calm manner made the passengers feel comfortable.

The boatman told us how the river changes with the seasons. We carried our own drinking water and kept our bags away from the edge. After a peaceful journey, we reached the other bank, where our relatives welcomed us. I enjoyed the scenery and learned that a river is both a beautiful part of nature and an important route for local people. The memory of the trip still makes me happy.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Winter Morning” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Winter Morning

A winter morning has a special beauty in Bangladesh. The air is cool, and fog often covers fields, roads and trees. People may wake to find drops of dew on grass and spiderwebs.

In villages, farmers begin their work despite the cold. Some people gather around a small fire to warm themselves. As the sun rises, the fog slowly disappears and the surroundings become clearer. Families may enjoy warm pitha and date juice where these are available and safely prepared.

On the way to school, I enjoy watching sunlight appear through the mist. People walk briskly in sweaters and shawls, and shops gradually open for the day. By noon, the warmth of the sun makes the morning cold seem like a distant memory.

Winter is pleasant for many people, but it can be difficult for those who lack warm clothes or shelter. We can share clean blankets and clothing through trustworthy local groups. We should also take care around fires and help younger children stay warm. A winter morning is memorable not only for its natural beauty but also for the kindness it can inspire among neighbours.

items.text: Write a short composition on “My Aim in Life” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
My Aim in Life

Everyone needs a goal to give direction to hard work. My aim is to become a doctor and serve people who have difficulty getting medical care. This ambition grew when I saw how a kind doctor patiently explained treatment to a worried family.

A doctor must have knowledge, practical skills and compassion. To prepare, I need to study science carefully, develop good habits and learn to communicate clearly. I should also listen to teachers and ask questions when I do not understand a lesson. Becoming a doctor takes many years of education and supervised training, so I must be ready to work steadily.

A good doctor must continue learning even after qualifying, because medical knowledge and treatments change. Just as importantly, patients need clear explanations and privacy. I hope to develop these qualities along with scientific knowledge so that people can feel heard and respected.

I hope one day to serve in a community where medical services are limited. I would treat patients with respect and encourage them to seek reliable health advice. My goal may be difficult, but it motivates me to use my time well. Whatever profession I finally choose, I want my work to benefit others.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A School Sports Day” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A School Sports Day

Our annual school sports day is one of the happiest events of the year. It brings students, teachers and families together and gives everyone a chance to enjoy games and friendly competition.

Before the event, teachers prepare the field and explain the rules. Students practise races and other activities suitable for their age. On the day itself, the programme begins with a welcome speech. Some students take part in running events, while others cheer for their classmates. Teachers supervise the activities and make sure that drinking water and first aid are available.

Our classmates who are not competing can help by welcoming visitors or recording results. Such roles are important because a successful event depends on many people. Including different kinds of activities also allows more students to participate according to their abilities and interests.

Winning a prize is exciting, but participation matters too. Players learn to respect rules, accept results and congratulate one another. At the end, prizes are distributed and everyone thanks the organisers. The event shows that sport is not only about winning; it also builds confidence, cooperation and friendship. I look forward to it every year.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Learning English” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Learning English

English is an international language used in education, business and communication. Learning it can help us read books, understand useful information and communicate with people from different countries. It also gives students access to many learning resources.

Learning English does not mean neglecting Bangla or any other language. Our mother tongue is central to our identity, and knowing more than one language is an advantage. To improve English, we should practise reading, writing, listening and speaking regularly. Simple stories, conversations and class activities can make practice enjoyable.

Listening to a short conversation and repeating useful expressions can improve pronunciation and understanding. Writing a few sentences about daily life is another practical exercise. Regular practice is more helpful than trying to memorise many unfamiliar words in a single evening.

Mistakes are a natural part of learning. Instead of being afraid, students should ask for help and try again. Keeping a vocabulary notebook and using new words in sentences can be useful. With patience and regular practice, we can become more confident. English is a practical skill that can open opportunities while allowing us to share our own culture with others.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Visit to a Historical Place” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Visit to a Historical Place

Last year I visited the historic city of Bagerhat with my family. I had read about its old buildings and was eager to see one of them. We visited the Sixty Dome Mosque, a famous example of Bengal's architectural heritage.

The building impressed me with its thick walls, rows of pillars and many domes. A guide explained that it was associated with Khan Jahan Ali and the medieval settlement of Khalifatabad. I listened carefully and tried to imagine the people who had lived and worked in the area centuries ago.

Before our visit, I looked at a map to understand where Bagerhat is located. Afterwards, I shared my notes with classmates and checked details in a reliable reference book. Learning about a place before and after a visit makes the experience more meaningful.

Visitors should respect a historical site. We avoided writing on the walls, put our rubbish in a bin and followed the rules at the entrance. The visit made history feel more real than a list of dates in a textbook. Such places help us understand earlier communities and their skills. Protecting them allows future generations to learn from them too.

items.text: Write a short composition on “My Favourite Game” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
My Favourite Game

My favourite game is football. It is played by two teams, each trying to score by sending the ball into the opponent's goal. I like it because it is energetic and requires cooperation.

I usually play with friends in a nearby field after school. Before starting, we agree on the boundaries and make sure the ground is reasonably safe. We pass the ball, defend together and encourage players who are still learning. When a disagreement occurs, we try to settle it calmly instead of arguing.

We take turns in different positions so that everyone can learn to attack and defend. Sometimes we practise passing before starting a match. These simple exercises help us understand that careful preparation and communication are as important as individual skill.

Football helps me exercise and teaches me to think quickly. More importantly, it reminds me that a team succeeds when its members support one another. A good player respects opponents and accepts the referee's decision. We take breaks and drink water, especially in hot weather. Whether our team wins or loses, I enjoy the time spent with my friends and the lessons learned on the field.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Honesty” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Honesty

Honesty means speaking the truth and acting without deception. It is an important quality because trust grows when people know that they can depend on one another. An honest person admits mistakes instead of hiding them.

Students can practise honesty in many ordinary situations. They should complete their own work, avoid cheating and return something they find to its owner or a responsible adult. If they damage a friend's property, they should explain what happened and try to put it right. Telling the truth may sometimes be uncomfortable, but a lie can create greater problems later.

For example, if I forget to complete a task, I should explain the reason rather than invent an excuse. An apology does not erase every consequence, but it is a first step towards correcting the problem. People can trust us more when our actions match our words.

Honesty should be combined with kindness. We can express a difficult truth politely and avoid hurting someone unnecessarily. Families, teachers and leaders can set examples by keeping promises and accepting responsibility. No one is perfect, but we can all make honest choices. Such choices build strong friendships and a more trustworthy society.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Life of a Farmer” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Life of a Farmer

A farmer plays an essential role in society by producing food and other crops. In Bangladesh, many farmers work in fields, orchards or vegetable gardens. Their work requires knowledge, effort and careful attention to the seasons.

A farmer prepares the soil, selects seeds and plants at a suitable time. Crops need water and protection from weeds and pests. Weather, floods, droughts and changes in prices can make farming uncertain. At harvest time, the farmer gathers the crop and arranges for it to be sold or stored.

Agriculture involves many people, including those who transport, process and sell crops. Women as well as men contribute to this work, although their efforts are not always equally recognised. Understanding the whole journey from field to table can help us value food more deeply.

Farmers can benefit from reliable information, fair access to markets and suitable tools. Responsible use of water and soil helps protect the land for the future. Consumers should respect their work and avoid wasting food. Whenever I eat a meal, I try to remember the many people who helped produce it. A farmer's contribution deserves recognition and support.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Day at a Village Fair” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Day at a Village Fair

A village fair is a colourful event that brings people together. I visited one with my family during a local festival. We arrived in the afternoon and found the open ground full of stalls and visitors.

Some stalls sold clay pots, toys, baskets and handmade ornaments. Others offered traditional snacks. I watched a craftsperson shape a small object and admired the patience required. Children enjoyed simple games while adults met friends and neighbours. We stayed together in the crowd and agreed on a meeting place in case anyone became separated.

The fair was also an opportunity to see skills passed from one generation to another. I asked a seller how long it took to make a basket, and she explained the process. Her answer made me appreciate the work behind an everyday object.

My favourite purchase was a small clay bird. We also listened to local music before returning home. A fair gives artisans and traders an opportunity to sell their goods, and it keeps local traditions alive. At the same time, organisers should provide clean facilities and manage crowds safely. The visit was enjoyable because it combined entertainment, craftsmanship and community spirit.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Punctuality” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Punctuality

Punctuality means doing things at the right time. A punctual person respects both personal responsibilities and other people's time. It is a habit that can be developed through planning and practice.

A student who reaches school on time can attend the whole lesson and settle down before class begins. Preparing books and clothes the night before may prevent a rushed morning. A simple timetable can also help us complete homework without leaving everything until the last moment. However, unexpected illness, transport problems or family difficulties can delay anyone, so we should respond to others with understanding.

A timetable should include reasonable breaks and enough sleep, not just a list of tasks. If a plan proves unrealistic, we can adjust it rather than give up. Over time, small improvements in planning can reduce stress and make important commitments easier to keep.

Punctuality is valuable in workplaces and public services too. When a meeting or journey begins on time, everyone can plan more effectively. We should allow extra time for possible delays and inform others if we cannot arrive as promised. Being punctual does not mean being hurried all the time; it means managing our duties thoughtfully.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Village Doctor” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Village Doctor

A village doctor is often a familiar figure in a rural community. People may turn to a local health worker when they are ill or need advice. Access to safe, qualified medical care is especially important where hospitals are far away.

A trained doctor listens to a patient's symptoms, examines the patient when necessary and recommends appropriate care. Some problems require tests or treatment at a hospital. A responsible practitioner recognises these limits and refers patients to a qualified facility when needed. Patients should not take antibiotics or other medicines without proper medical advice.

A community health clinic can provide a place for trained staff to offer advice and arrange referrals. Clear information about opening hours and available services helps families know where to go. Transport and affordable treatment are also important, especially during an emergency.

Health workers can also encourage vaccination, hygiene and safe drinking water. Their work becomes easier when communities have good roads, clinics and reliable supplies. We should appreciate compassionate service while checking a practitioner's qualifications. A healthy village needs both caring professionals and a health system that people can reach and trust.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Rainy Season in Bangladesh” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Rainy Season in Bangladesh

The rainy season brings a major change to life in Bangladesh. Dark clouds gather, and frequent rain fills ponds, rivers and fields. The countryside becomes green, and many farmers welcome the water needed for crops.

Rain also provides relief from the summer heat. Children enjoy watching raindrops fall, while boats become useful in some waterlogged areas. However, heavy rain can create serious problems. Roads may become muddy or flooded, classes may be interrupted, and low-lying homes can be damaged. Floods can also make safe drinking water harder to obtain.

During the rains, families often keep an umbrella or raincoat ready before leaving home. Farmers watch the weather closely because both too little and too much rain can affect crops. The season reminds us how closely daily routines are connected to nature.

Communities can prepare by keeping drains clear, listening to official warnings and helping vulnerable neighbours reach safe places. We should avoid floodwater where possible because it may hide dangers or contamination. The rainy season is therefore a time of beauty as well as caution. Careful preparation helps people enjoy its benefits and face its difficulties.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Street Hawker” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Street Hawker

A street hawker sells goods by moving from place to place or standing near a busy street. A hawker may carry fruit, toys, household items or other small products. This work is familiar in many towns and villages.

The hawker often begins early and spends long hours attracting customers. Buyers appreciate being able to purchase useful goods near their homes. For the seller, each sale contributes to daily income. The work can be difficult in rain, heat or heavy traffic, and earnings may vary from day to day.

Some hawkers know their regular customers and bring goods that people request. A friendly greeting can make a short purchase feel personal. We should bargain respectfully and remember that the seller must cover costs as well as earn a living.

Hawkers deserve respect and safe working conditions. At the same time, selling areas should be arranged so that pedestrians, including people with disabilities, can move safely. Food sellers need access to clean water and hygienic facilities. A practical arrangement should consider the needs of both sellers and the public. The street hawker's work shows the importance of small businesses in everyday life.

items.text: Write a short composition on “My Favourite Teacher” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
My Favourite Teacher

A good teacher can inspire students to learn and become better people. My favourite teacher is our English teacher, who combines clear explanations with patience and kindness.

In class, she begins a lesson with a question and invites us to share our ideas. She reads stories aloud and helps us notice new words in context. When we make mistakes, she explains how to improve instead of making us feel ashamed. She also encourages quiet students to participate, while allowing them time to think.

She also asks us to read beyond the textbook and discuss what we learn. Sometimes she admits that a question needs further research, showing us that teachers continue learning too. This honesty makes the classroom a place where questions are welcome.

What I admire most is her fairness. She listens to different opinions and treats students with respect. She reminds us to be honest in our work and helpful to our classmates. Her lessons have made me more confident about speaking English. I know that learning requires my own effort, but her guidance makes that effort enjoyable. I hope to follow her example of patience and responsibility.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Benefits of Morning Walks” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Benefits of Morning Walks

A morning walk can be a refreshing way to begin the day. The air may feel cooler, and familiar streets or fields look different in the early light. Walking regularly can also be part of a healthy routine.

I sometimes walk with a family member along a safe path near our home. We choose a comfortable pace and wear suitable shoes. During the walk we notice birds, trees and people beginning their daily work. After returning, I feel ready to wash, eat breakfast and prepare for school.

A walk with a friend or family member can also provide time for conversation. We do not need to cover a long distance to enjoy the experience. Starting gently and choosing a regular time can make the habit easier to maintain.

A walk should be adapted to a person's health and circumstances. A busy road, poor lighting or unsafe weather may make another time or place a better choice. People with health concerns can seek advice from a qualified professional. Walking alone cannot replace good food and adequate sleep, but it is a simple activity that many people can enjoy. A regular walk can benefit both body and mind.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Visit to a Zoo” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Visit to a Zoo

During a school holiday, I visited a zoo with my family. I was excited to see animals I had previously known only from books and pictures. At the entrance, we read the visitor rules and planned our route.

We saw several kinds of birds, deer and other animals. A keeper explained why animals need suitable food, shelter and space. I enjoyed watching their different movements, but I also realised that wild animals have complex needs that cannot always be met easily in captivity.

I later read more about one of the animals we saw and learned about threats to its natural habitat. This helped me understand that protecting wildlife involves land, water and communities as well as individual animals. A visit can be a beginning rather than the end of learning.

We did not feed the animals or throw objects into their enclosures. Instead, we observed quietly and kept the grounds clean. A responsible zoo should protect animal welfare and help visitors learn about conservation. Protecting natural habitats is equally important because animals belong to wider ecosystems. The visit was enjoyable, but it also taught me to think carefully about our responsibilities towards other living creatures.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Good Manners” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Good Manners

Good manners are ways of showing respect and consideration for others. Saying please and thank you, listening without interrupting and speaking politely can make everyday interactions more pleasant.

Manners begin at home but are useful everywhere. At school, students can greet teachers, wait their turn and help keep shared spaces clean. On public transport, offering a seat to someone who needs it is a thoughtful act. Online, good manners include avoiding hurtful messages and respecting other people's privacy.

Apologising when we have caused inconvenience is another useful habit. On the other hand, a polite manner should never be used to hide unfair behaviour. Real courtesy includes helping people feel safe and included, even when nobody is watching.

Politeness does not mean agreeing with everything. We can express disagreement honestly without insulting another person. We should also remember that customs differ and that a person's disability or circumstances may affect how they communicate. The purpose of manners is not to judge people by rigid rules, but to make others feel respected. Small acts of courtesy can build trust and make a community more welcoming.

items.text: Write a short composition on “My First Day at School” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
My First Day at School

I still remember my first day at a new school. I felt excited, but I was also nervous because I did not know the teachers or the other students. My parent accompanied me to the gate and encouraged me to be brave.

A teacher welcomed the new students and showed us our classroom. I chose a seat beside a child who smiled and introduced herself. During the first lesson, we learned the names of our teachers and talked about the subjects we would study. At break time, my new friend showed me where to find drinking water and the library.

When I returned home, I told my family about the classroom and the new people I had met. The next morning I still felt a little uncertain, but I knew where to go. Each day became easier as familiar faces and routines appeared.

By the end of the day, my fear had become curiosity. I understood that many other students were nervous too. The kindness of my teacher and classmate helped me feel that I belonged. That day taught me how important a warm welcome can be for someone entering an unfamiliar place.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Education” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Education

Education helps people develop knowledge, skills and judgment. It allows us to understand the world, communicate with others and make informed choices. Learning takes place at school, at home and throughout life.

At school, students study language, mathematics, science and many other subjects. They also learn to cooperate, solve problems and ask questions. A good education should encourage curiosity rather than mere memorisation. Teachers, families and communities all have a role in supporting learners.

Unfortunately, poverty, disability, unsafe travel or other barriers may prevent children from attending school. Making education accessible requires safe buildings, supportive teachers and attention to different needs. Students can contribute by respecting classmates and sharing resources responsibly.

Education can also help people recognise misleading claims and take part in discussions about their communities. Different learners progress in different ways, so patient support matters. A classroom where questions are welcomed gives students confidence to continue learning beyond examinations.

Education alone cannot solve every social problem, but it gives people tools to participate and improve their lives. When everyone has a fair chance to learn, the whole community benefits from their ideas and abilities.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Flood in Our Area” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Flood in Our Area

A flood can change ordinary life very quickly. In this imagined account, heavy rain caused the river near our area to rise above its banks. Water entered roads and some homes, and many families had to leave for safer places.

My family listened to local announcements and packed important documents, drinking water and essential medicines. We moved to a designated shelter with our neighbours. Volunteers helped elderly people and children, while local workers shared information about food and safe water. We stayed away from electrical wires and did not walk through fast-moving water.

Not every family experienced the flood in the same way. Some had lost crops, while others needed help cleaning or replacing school materials. Listening to each family's needs helped volunteers provide more useful support instead of assuming that everyone required the same thing.

After the water went down, families returned to assess the damage. Cleaning homes and repairing belongings took time. The experience showed how important early warnings, safe shelters and community cooperation are. Floods can cause great suffering, but preparation and mutual help can reduce risks. We should support recovery and learn from each event.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Picnic I Enjoyed” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Picnic I Enjoyed

Last winter our class went on a picnic with our teachers. We travelled to a park outside town and spent a pleasant day playing, eating and exploring together. Everyone was excited when we gathered at school in the morning.

Before leaving, the teachers counted the students and explained the safety rules. At the park, we spread mats in a shaded area and shared the food we had brought. Later we played games, sang songs and walked along a marked path. A teacher helped organise a friendly quiz, and even those who did not win enjoyed taking part.

We planned the picnic in advance and brought only what we needed. Sharing food allowed us to taste different dishes, and we checked that everyone had something suitable to eat. Our teachers' careful planning helped us enjoy the day without forgetting safety.

Before going home, we collected our rubbish and checked that no belongings were left behind. The return journey was quieter because everyone was tired. The picnic gave us a welcome break from our usual routine and helped us know our classmates better. Its happiest lesson was that a simple day becomes special when people cooperate and care for one another.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Saving Water” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Saving Water

Water is necessary for drinking, cooking, farming and cleanliness. Although rain and rivers are familiar in Bangladesh, safe water is not always available where and when people need it. Saving water and protecting its sources are therefore important.

At home, we can turn off a tap while brushing our teeth and repair leaks promptly. We can use only the water needed for washing and reuse suitable water for plants when it is safe to do so. Farmers and communities can also plan irrigation carefully to reduce waste.

A leaking tap may seem unimportant, but it can waste water day after day. Telling an adult or the person responsible for maintenance is more useful than ignoring it. We should also avoid contaminating shared water points while collecting or storing water.

Saving water is not enough if sources become polluted. Rubbish, sewage and harmful chemicals should not be allowed to enter ponds and rivers. Local authorities and communities share responsibility for safe water systems. Children can help by reporting a leaking tap and keeping their surroundings clean. Small daily actions, combined with effective public services, can protect this essential resource for the future.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A Memorable Birthday” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A Memorable Birthday

My last birthday was memorable not because of expensive gifts, but because of the time I spent with my family and friends. We decided to celebrate simply at home after school.

My younger sister helped decorate the room with paper shapes. My parents prepared a favourite meal, and a few friends came in the afternoon. We played a guessing game and shared a cake. One friend gave me a handmade card containing a poem, which made me smile. We also took some food to a neighbour who could not join us.

The handmade card became my favourite reminder of the day. I kept it on my desk and read the poem again later. It showed that a personal effort can mean more than a costly present, especially when it expresses a genuine friendship.

At the end of the celebration, everyone helped clear the table and put away the decorations. I felt grateful for the effort people had made to be together. The day reminded me that happiness does not depend on spending a great deal of money. Thoughtful words, shared laughter and kindness can make an ordinary room feel very special.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Importance of Road Safety” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Importance of Road Safety

Road safety is a shared responsibility. Pedestrians, drivers, passengers and authorities all have roles in reducing accidents. Careful behaviour and safe road design can protect lives.

Pedestrians should use footpaths and marked crossings where available. Before crossing, they should look carefully in both directions and avoid being distracted by a phone. Children may need help from an adult on busy roads. Passengers should wait in a safe place and avoid boarding a moving vehicle.

Drivers should obey speed limits, follow traffic signals and never drive while distracted or impaired. Authorities can improve safety by maintaining roads, providing crossings and enforcing traffic rules fairly. Schools can teach students how to identify hazards and practise safe travel.

At school, a supervised discussion can help students identify dangerous places near the gate. They can share their observations with teachers, who may raise concerns with the appropriate authorities. Safe routes need attention from the whole community, not just individual travellers.

No single action can prevent every accident, and people do not always have access to safe infrastructure. Nevertheless, attention, planning and cooperation can make journeys safer for everyone. We should treat road safety as a daily duty rather than an occasional concern.

items.text: Write a short composition on “A School Magazine” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
A School Magazine

A school magazine is a collection of writing and artwork produced by students and teachers. It may include poems, stories, essays, drawings and reports about school activities. The magazine gives young writers a chance to share their ideas.

To prepare an issue, an editorial team invites contributions and selects suitable work. Teachers can help students correct language and check facts without removing their individual voices. Contributors should submit their own work or acknowledge any material they use with permission. The team then organises the pages and checks the final copy before publication.

Students can learn useful skills by interviewing people, planning deadlines and revising drafts. They also learn to accept suggestions without taking criticism personally. When the finished issue appears, contributors can take pride in the teamwork that made it possible.

A magazine encourages creativity, cooperation and careful reading. A student who is shy in class may find confidence through a poem or illustration. A printed or digital edition can also preserve memories of the school year. If everyone has a fair opportunity to contribute, the magazine becomes a lively record of the whole school community.

items.text: Write a short composition on “The Uses and Abuses of the Internet” in about 250 words.
items.explanation:
Sample composition:
The Uses and Abuses of the Internet

The internet connects people to information and services across the world. Students can use it to attend lessons, consult reference materials and communicate with teachers. It also helps people find news, conduct business and stay in touch with relatives.

However, not everything online is reliable. False information can spread quickly, so important claims should be checked against trustworthy sources. Spending too much time on games or social media can also interfere with sleep and study. Online strangers may try to trick people into sharing personal information.

A website can look convincing even when its information is inaccurate. Checking the author, date and evidence, and comparing claims with other reliable sources, helps readers make better judgments. We should be especially cautious before sharing alarming messages or financial information.

We should use strong passwords, keep them private and ask a trusted adult for help when something seems suspicious. It is wise to think before posting and to treat others respectfully. A balanced schedule leaves time for study, exercise and family. The internet is a useful tool when we use it carefully, critically and with respect for our own safety and that of others.
